title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
content:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals.
Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
Future versions of Siri will be able to control third-party apps and perform more complex tasks.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.
But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says:
Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

report.summary: Apple is reportedly accelerating Siri’s roadmap to add deeper app control and long-running agentic capabilities as rivals ship more capable AI agents.
report.background: Siri launched in 2011 as an early voice assistant, but the generative AI boom reset expectations for what assistants can do. Apple introduced Apple Intelligence and promised a more capable Siri, yet many advanced features have arrived slowly or been delayed. Meanwhile, competitors such as OpenAI, Meta, and xAI have pushed toward “agentic” systems that can track goals and complete multi-step tasks with less user prompting. According to the report, Apple leadership is now pressing software chief Craig Federighi to speed up Siri’s roadmap, fearing the company is falling behind rivals even after shipping a functional Siri AI update on a short timeline.
key_points: Siri’s next near-term upgrade is expected to give it fine-grained control over Apple’s own apps. Reported examples include rotating and cropping images in Photos and organizing Safari tabs. That capability is said to be planned for iOS 27.3, making Siri more useful for everyday device actions rather than just answering questions.

A larger change is expected in the spring: integration with third-party apps. This would let Siri perform actions such as placing a Grubhub order or booking a dinner reservation through OpenTable. It would turn Siri from an information assistant into a system that can act across the app ecosystem.

Apple ultimately wants Siri to become truly agentic, meaning it can pursue ongoing goals, decide what step comes next, and continue working without the user initiating every action. The report says this direction could arrive as early as next year, driven by consumer expectations and competitive pressure.

Internally, the report says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Siri’s roadmap. Apple has delivered a functional Siri AI version quickly, but it reportedly has no illusion that it is keeping pace with rivals such as OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and xAI’s Grok.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Apple’s push confirms that agentic assistants are becoming the next battleground, shifting competition from chatbots to systems that can take actions across apps and services. For developers, deeper Siri integration could create new distribution opportunities, but it will also require robust App Intents, permissions, and workflows designed for automated actions. For regular users, the payoff could be more hands-free convenience and multi-step automation, but trust will be critical: users will need clear confirmations, privacy controls, and predictable behavior before letting an assistant place orders, book reservations, or manage personal data. Apple’s advantage is its tight control of the OS and app ecosystem, but execution speed and reliability will determine whether Siri can close the gap.
report.tools: Developers should watch Apple’s App Intents, SiriKit, and Shortcuts frameworks, which are likely surfaces for exposing app actions to Siri. For agent prototyping, open-source options such as LangGraph, AutoGen, and Open Interpreter can help teams test goal-tracking and multi-step workflows. Readers tracking competitors should follow OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and xAI’s Grok as reference points for agentic assistant design.
